data: A very solid game the puzzles are a lot of fun and the combat is decent, overall the atmosphere is amazing highly recommend playing
, it's definitely worth the difficulty and *absolutely* worth every penny
It's so good, beautiful and challenging, I love it
Great game with amazing visuals, gameplay and music, if you like unique mechanics and tons of secrets, 100% recommended
the gameplay itself is just disappointing
- exploration is boring and punishing due to level design and lack of lore
then half the time your character is entirely obscured and you can't even see if there is even anything there
I actually don't care because I already know the core gameplay is atrocious
Rather challenging bosses (requiring countless tries or brute forcing) and overly cryptic puzzles (that are a chore to solve)
I don't think the combat itself is bad, and the lock-on only occasionally caused problems when fighting groups
There's a difference between making a game challenging and making a game tedious, repetitive, and unfair
The difficulty itself isn't always the problem
, the difficulty quickly ramps up unnecessarily without giving the player anything in return
Tldr: battle is repetitive and unfun, exploration is slow and annoying, the game doesn't want you to use the features it has
I gave a cursory look online and some claim the puzzles only start in the endgame… that is just bad game design
Sadly, I'm at the endgame and just lost the will to finish it
kinda leaves no motivation behind what you're doing in terms of your quest (little to no NPC dialogue either)
There's not much of a story to speak of, which is fine
The game barely tells you where to go, and because the manual is mostly written in an invented language, you're often just guessing from pictures

What a game. WHAT A GAAAAAAAME.
I didn't know a whole lot about the game going in and I was so pleasantly surprised! Tunic is wonderful, everything that is seeks to do it does well. Puzzles? Incredible. Music? Amazing. Art? Gave me a reason to live. Gameplay? Kept me entertained for hours (I got lost a lot). Little fox? I would die for him.
While playing Tunic I had it on my mind 24/7 and would take any break I could to play it, it is so good to see a game with this level of love put into it, I wish I could look at everyone who made this game possible and just hug them super tight and say "THANK YOU, I REALLY LIKED THAT"

10000000/10

This game has been an interesting experience. in the beginning, it can be frustrating and unnecessarily difficult, but learning and experimenting with the mechanics is a wonderful experience. I don't recommend playing without a controller though, as the keyboard can feel uncomfortable and difficult

One of the best experiences I have had with a game, especially in the Metroidvania and Soulsborne genres. Every part of the world is a mystery and trying to figure out what is going on is a wonderful experience. I have purposely avoided any knowledge of the game as per recommendations of friends and I am glad I did.

This game is what I would call an "epic" in reference to the range of emotion that it made me feel. Seriously incredible. The soundtrack, alone, I have listened to so many times over. The game, I've played twice over already. I need to go further. I'm not done yet.

I HAVE NOT COMPLETED THIS GAME

I can’t, I’m not good enough : /

I don’t normally play games like this but I have to say I enjoyed a majority of the 8 hours I played.

This game does a wonderful job of allowing you to explore all the nooks and crannies of a limited world yourself, and provides visual context clues that repeatedly had me going “OHHH”.

Enemy patterns aren’t too difficult to figure out, and after upgrading a bit it becomes less of a threat to mess up.

I unfortunately had to stop the game when it said “Get Gud”.

Light spoilers ahead.

You will get a point in the story where it caps your health, stamina, and mana. Further, the enemies you will fight can reduce your stats if you get hit.

Banging my head against a wall for an hour to finish a single fight isn’t my style, and it’s not really how I get enjoyment out of a game.

I imagine Souls players will find it a relaxing breath of a game, and I still highly recommend it.

There's not much I can say in a review without spoiling anything, but I will at least say that starting the game off as a mysterious adventure and having the game progression turn on its head by the end of the game is undoubtedly wild (in a fantastic way). And to really top it off, the puzzle solving all throughout this game is some of the most satisfying I've ever solved. It's the type of thing that makes you get a notepad and pencil out for notes and everything in between, and I love it.

TUNIC instills a true sense of wonder.

It's fantastic. Don't read around here for too long, I'm sure you'll spoil yourself in no time. This is another Outer Wilds situation.

If the question "What if the Legend of Zelda had a deep sense of mystery to its world, that you can explore and solve entirely through engaging with the game" sounds at all appealing to you, then you should play TUNIC right now, before anyone can spoil those mysteries for you.

We all understand that video games can be art at this point. But for the most part, we think about that question from a narrative, or at minimum aesthetic, perspective: can a video game have a story that makes it art? Can a video game's music, or visual style, be worthy of artistic criticism?

The far more challenging hurdle has always been this: can a video game's mechanics, its level architecture and structure, the design itself, be considered art?

The answer, dear reader, is yes.

The answer, dear reader, is Tunic .
Easily the best game from the last 10+ years. It really captures the magic of old Zelda games but does its own thing too. The soundtrack is also a masterpiece.

Game looks gorgeous, plays really well, has awesome items and abilities, secret puzzles are great.

It's a game where you keep discovering how the world works and you get to use that knowledge for your benefit, similar to Outer wilds.

Does not suffer from it's forced camera angle, even though I spent a lot of time running into walls, but it's fun when you find a secret.

What an experience!
The game immediately gave me Zelda vibes and activated all my nostalgia neurons, but it's a lot more than it seems. A more accurate description would be if Dark Souls and Legend of Zelda had a child who wears Link's face as a mask and cranks the cryptic puzzles up to 11.
The challenges are always fair, rarely frustrating. There's always a hint somewhere and it feels hella satisfying if you find it yourself.

Don't forget to RTFM, not only if you're stuck.

Please give us Tunic 2! :)

Very fun game. early-mid game can be a bit frustrating as you are still trying to figure out what things are/where to go due to the cryptic language. It's also pretty easy to miss some pathways due to camera angles etc (I missed one and ended up running around for 2 hours when I just needed to run against a wall I had not yet run against), but if you can make it into the later game and unlock more abilities/access the late game puzzles, its a much more pleasant experience

A relatively short game, but I was completely lost in it from start to finish. I went into this totally blind and was blown away by the puzzles. I won't spoil anything, but just assure people that aren't super into puzzles that you don't need to do any of the hard ones to beat the game. If all you want to do is complete it, then it's mostly just a simple combat game. But, wow, what a unique experience this was. Truly something special.

And for people that are super into puzzles, it seriously rewards those looking for its much deeper secrets...

One of the best games I've played in years by far.

If you are gonna play this game DO NOT USE GUIDES, it will spoil you of things you are not even looking for.

Being an avid gamer doesn't help when you try to find a game that suits you, this one stroke a nerve I didnt even knew I have.

I had fun every second of it, every secret, every puzzle, every page found was a joyful experience, felt even better than playing the original Link to the Past back in the 90s.

I dont review games, like ever. This game here tho deserves more than a good review in my opinion, it deserves a THANK YOU to the devs, for making something so clearly done with love, it must have been hard af to put together something like this.

I imagine it will be difficult to top and I don't pretend to find a game like this prolly ever, but for now I'm gonna replay it and I imagine I'll be doing so many times from now on, one of those games you repeat once a year or so.

Thank you, and congrats on the amazing job!
I probably need to go through this game again, but it's pretty great and very adorable.

The game is very cute and fun and I would recommend it. I found the in-game guide very fun with its fictional language and puzzles.

However, I found myself not knowing what to do quite often and looking online for answers because I don't want to walk around the whole world again. At the start of the game I missed getting the shield because it simply lets you walk past wherever it's hidden and continue with the game. I think it could instruct you on what to do better and make it so the shield and other important items won't ever be missed by the player.

This game is great! I had been following it for a while before release and playing some of the demos and that really got me hyped. After release, I can say it was even better than I imagined. It's cryptic nature and hard but fun battles make it a very good game to play at least once for anyone who likes a challenge.

This game is absolutely beautiful! The story is mysterious, the graphics are very cute and nostalgic of older RPG games, resembling the initial LOZ games, and the music and sound effectcs throughout the game are astounding. This game has me hooked!

Such a gem of a game, its songs and overall vibes are immaculate and the feeling of solving a puzzle or understanding whatever is written between the lines is addictive.
Price tag a little steep and the combat can get a little frustrating at times, but i think it`s worth it ~ 9/10

After three decades of gaming, this is the game I wish I could play again for the first time more than any other. Simple yet challenging souls-like combat wrapped in a cozy vibrant aesthetic that evoked feelings of wonder and nostalgia I was surprised I could even still experience from modern titles.

Do yourself a favor and go into this one blind. Knowledge is literal power in this world and the feeling of accomplishment from solving the multitude of puzzles seamlessly embedded in the environment is unfortunately a one-time experience that should not be missed.
Puzzle when game is confusing because when puzzle happen very hard to do puzzle and figure out puzzle game to have puzzle in game MANUAL pages to play puzzles to solve. Quite fun, I must say.

There's a lot to like about Tunic, but it has, and I am not exaggerating, some of the worst combat I've ever played in a video game. It is not fun. The exploration and discovery stuff is neat, I'm intrigued about the world. But actually playing the game is completely miserable. I quite like isometric combat too. The problem is that it's poorly made, unforgivably so. I'll be honest, I'll probably take another crack at it because there are things I like about the game. But, moment to moment, interacting with it, I am not having any fun at all.

Incredible game, i'm in love with it definetly in my top 3 :O !
To be honest, only few games reach this level of deepness and creativity but staying playable for anyone.
Maybe some secrets of the game will be hard to find for you, but never give up or ask a friend who have done it ! It's so perfect game, i truly love it and i'm always at the beginning ! Tunic Team really well done for what you created <3
The game is beautiful and it's really satisfying playing your game !

This game feels quite different. People called it classic style which I believe so because there are very few hand holdings up to the point you have to find and check the guide. I fought Siege Engine without any upgrades and felt it was wrong somehow and then searched for how to upgrade. Life got easier after that. 

The graphics is unique, looks a lot like Zelda Link Awakening. Puzzles are hidden quite well and requiring attention.
This game is amazing, as a souls-like, as an adventure game and more. The music, the art direction, everything is really fascinating
A very cut game that feels a lot like Zelda with a lot of puzzles and the occasional Dark Souls boss. Greatly recommended for those who like figuring out puzzles and seeing clever map design.

Tunic was by far the best game I played all year
Going into this game I was expecting a cute isometric classic zelda styled game with souls combat mechanics, and that's pretty much exactly what I got, until tunic pulled back the veil and revealed that the true game was something much more than that, something that had me scratching my head for days laying in bed theorising and dotting my desk with dozens of notes, very few games ask that of the player and for this Tunic is truly something special.

Great graphics and music, the combat is good enough to keep you engaged. The coolest part about the game is the puzzles and the game book, it feels like playing a zelda game again as a kid. You will be confused, if you need help look up guides or tips carefully so you don't get spoiled.

I don't understand how this game can be so perfect. I'm watching the trailer play as I try and write this review and the emotions are coming rushing back to me.

I strongly strongly reccommend not looking anything up online. Read the manual, keep a stack of scrap paper. Leave it and come back to it. Discuss it with a friend. This is a game that will reward you so much if you play it on its own terms. I think it's pretty great in any case, but there's just so much here!

This game sets out to contain 0 dialog of any kind, only working through map queues and clues. And I think it did well. I also think this exists in the same category as Death's Door, and I enjoyed that one a little more. But I still happily beat this one and I think its cult following is well earned. It's unique and does what nobody else has - I commend it for it.

Finally pushed through and finished this game and gosh. What an amazing experience, definitely comparable to Outer Wilds where knowledge makes up most of your progression

Play this game with a pen and some paper, and go in blind. It is an amazing game, where almost everything is locked under the same key: knowledge

Marvelous, marvelous game. It has that feeling of playing a game as a child, not fully understanding the rules yet, and when you turn to the instruction booklet to help you realize your mom accidentally got you the Japanese copy of the game so you can't actually read it. You make do with intuition and the pretty pictures.
This game is amazing. Mark my word. But you have to go in blind, If you are reading this comment you've already messed up. Stop right now, buy the game and experience it for yourself!

Nothing short of amazing! At least in regards to secrets, easer eggs and general game and graphics style, music and gameplay in general. Combat was not the most polished part of the game (overall, its simple but good, but a few parts can be very challenging... it's manageable but can be rather difficult for an average player). Thankfully, the game offers enough ways to push through the challenge (consumables, upgrades and such) and devs even included all the accessibility options one could ever want, including reduced combat difficulty and straight up invulnerability.

Some areas can be confusing at first glance. And at second look. And after an hour. Sometimes it's best to take a break and try again later with a fresh eye. If you can't progress at all, there is no shame in looking up hints or a solution to a particular problem, internet is full of hints for every puzzle, I believe.

Overall, I loved the game, despite a few challenging moments.

A whole lot of fun. It's a game about ah-ha! moments of discovery, where you learn about something you theoretically could've done the whole time. Given that, you might want to play it without looking anything up.

I think people put a bit too much emphasis on the "DON'T LOOK ANYTHING UP!" angle, though, because it implies that the secrets are what make the game good. This might be the case for a game like Void Stranger, where the secrets ARE the game, but TUNIC also happens to be a pretty great half-zelda-half-soulslike. The combat is fun. The music is fantastic. The worldbuilding is interesting.

Play TUNIC.

Great game. 
Definitely recommend to anyone who loves topdown Zelda games and enjoys discovering secrets and puzzles.
Please don't look up anything about this game before playing it, this is a game you must experience on your own.

I love this game so much.
The puzzles are incredible (especially the endgame ones!) and always manage to make me feel great after solving them. The combat can definitely feel lackluster at times (especially when fighting the Siege Engine; the collision between its body and legs felt too big when trying to closely circle around it ), but the beauty of a lot of the puzzles more than makes up for the combat's shortcomings. Some of the puzzles are definitely on the obscure side, but everything is reasonable to solve without any external help, which is always a great feature of any singleplayer puzzle-rich game. The art direction and music are both excellent.
If you love other puzzle-rich exploration games like Animal Well or FEZ, definitely give this a try. TUNIC is well worth the time and energy that I invested into it.

Tunic is a really fun game, I had a great time with it. Exploring feels rewarding, the puzzles are great, and there are plenty of secrets for anyone who enjoys finding them. I especially loved collecting the instruction manual and trying to make sense of it, it led to lots of "aha" moments.

Very good and surprisingly unique. Probably closest to something like Fez in spirit. Figuring out the puzzle to get the true ending was the highlight of the game. Recommended for those who enjoy using pen and paper to take notes while playing, and who are okay exploring and inferring where to go instead of being told.

Pretty fun, the late game stuff probably could have done a bit better with the hints as to what you are supposed to do, so I ended up looking up hints online a couple times. More of a souls-like with simple 2D Zelda style combat.
I had all major things spoiled for me, all the super secret stuff.... and this game is still filled with secrets and interesting to play. You lose this time, idiot trolls.

An incredible adventure game where realizing the solutions is one of the main game mechanics. The puzzle solving is top-tier in this game and while I couldn't understand everything on my own, especially with the much more difficult ones for secrets, what I solved felt real good. Deciphering the pages you collect for the illustrated manual and applying that knowledge to the puzzles you encounter pounded my brain with dopamine.

The combat can be tough at times, but it seemed manageable. I only truly had trouble with the final boss, but that's when I used the game's accessibility options to let me progress. I'll also mention that the sound design is also fantastic and made my headphones happy.

I hope to revisit this game to grab the true ending, but even if I don't, I'll remember it being well-crafted and heartfelt experience full of mystery and discovery.

This game is so good. At first I thought it was just a top down Zelda but with a fox, however it turned out even better. The battles are intense and difficult but fair. 10/10 every puzzle broke my mind more than the last one. Truly a masterpiece.

play this game if you enjoy overarching puzzles surrounding a fun (and difficult at times) exploratory experience. It's essentially Legend of Zelda-esque romp through a mysterious land that you'll need a pen and paper to decipher the secrets of. It's really, really good. I finished it once on switch, though I didn't 100% the game. Any amount of progression is tied to your puzzle solving skills, and when your arsenal reaches a certain point, you get rewarded for thinking laterally.

One of the most magical video game experiences I've ever had the pleasure of enjoying. It's hard, so you might want to turn down the combat settings (in advanced options) or turn on no fail mode (in accessibility). Neither of these take away from the enjoyment of the game, it's just as wonderful with them enabled as it is without.

Honestly,
TUNIC is the most impactful game I've ever played, you actually have to THINK in order to progress. You are also rewarded and FEEL rewarded If you solve a puzzle.

Don't know why people bash on the combat system, I thought it was quite rewarding once you got good at it.

The game also makes you slow down and not rush forward or give you sensory-overload with all the typical effects other games have.

All in all 11/10, do wish It would've lasted longer though...

Tunic is the most thought provoking and engaging game I have played in a long time. Initially it presents as a solid (but beautifully stylised) third person adventure with your normal attack/dodge/block core mechanics but slowly reveals itself to be much more.

The game starts without stifling you with a mandatory hand-holding tutorial segment - instead mechanics and the main quest are explained through interaction with the world and collecting mysterious manual pages for the player to interpret. This may sound daunting but worked seamlessly in practice. I never stalled on where to go and game progression was rewarding because it was entirely driven by the player's desire to explore.

Progression through the game comes in the form of upgrading your character, picking up new equipment and techniques and consequently being able to access new areas with new enemies. Normal enemies are typically only challenging in groups but the game operates off a system of checkpoint shrines so it is really a game of how many encounters you can endure while exploring. Game bosses were distinct, challenging, and were satisfyingly spectacular.

The game truly shines however on the depths of its puzzles and the evidently large amount of care the devs have put into them. The more you as a player are willing to invest to decode the manual and solve the various puzzles without looking at guides the more you will appreciate the game - I highly recommend playing with pens and paper handy.

2 hours in-

What do you mean this isn't an official Zelda game?

9 hours in-

A Link To the Past, was one of the key reasons I learned to read as a child. There was so many words I had never seen before. So many daunting paragraphs of text that I slowly, slowly began to understand, As I also slowly began to understand the world and story of Hyrule. Zelda's Plight and Link's Journey.

It wasn't until I started up Tunic that I realized how incredibly important that was to my experience, and probably the experience of so many other people who fell in love with that game. This feeling combined with the games magical presentation makes it a, IMO, masterpiece.

If you interested enough in Tunic to read the reviews, then yes, you want this game.

The combat is sh*t in this game, specially then you compare it with games like Death's Door. I want to play Zelda style game, but this games also clones mechanics from Souls games without even clue why they are there in the first place.

This game is honestly awesome. Very familiar being a Legend of Zelda type game while also being very innovative and unique. The exploration and world building are extremely satisfying and refreshing for a game in this genre. I especially love how the "tutorial" works in this game, where finding and unlocking parts of the game manual and then deciphering what you've found is an entire puzzle in itself. Very satisfying and I'm going to be watching this developer very closely for any future projects.

If you like Legend of Zelda style games and you're looking for something new, you can't go wrong with this. I'd say this game is well worth the $30 they're asking for it.

tldr.text: Very Positive (91%): players like the gameplay and the difficulty.
The combat draws the most complaints.

Content and grind complaints rose in recent reviews, and one reviewer says "battle is repetitive and unfun", so buyers who dislike repetition should weigh that.
